source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

fr.L: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée, disant :
fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée :
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a donné ce message :

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula, as in 1:3 and 17:1.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֔ם שָׂ֥א עַל־צֹ֖ר קִינָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, take up over Tyre a lament,

en.L: And you, son of man, take up a lament over Tyre,
en.B: Now you, son of man, raise a lament over Tyre,
en.R: Son of man, sing a funeral song about Tyre.

fr.L: Et toi, fils d’homme, entonne sur Tyr une complainte,
fr.B: Toi, fils d’homme, entonne une complainte sur Tyr,
fr.R: Fils d’homme, chante un chant de deuil sur Tyr.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: a lament: a funeral song
decisions.reason: See the note at 19:1. Ezekiel sings over Tyre as over the dead, though the city still stands: its end is certain.

decisions.choice: funeral song (R); lament (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable says what a lament was, as in 19:1.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לְצ֗וֹר הַיֹּשֶׁ֨בֶת֙ עַל־מְבוֹאֹ֣ת יָ֔ם רֹכֶ֨לֶת֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֶל־אִיִּ֖ים רַבִּ֑ים כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה צ֕וֹר אַ֣תְּ אָמַ֔רְתְּ אֲנִ֖י כְּלִ֥ילַת יֹֽפִי׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will say to Tyre, who sits at [the] entrances of [the] sea, the trader of the peoples to many coastlands: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Tyre, you have said, I [am] perfect of beauty.

en.L: and say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrances of the sea, \q the trader of the peoples to many coastlands, \q Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: \q Tyre, you have said, "I [am] perfect in beauty."
en.B: and say to Tyre, the city that sits at the gateways of the sea, \q trading with the peoples of many coastlands, \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: \q Tyre, you have said, "I am perfect in beauty."
en.R: Say to Tyre, the city at the harbor gates of the sea, \q which trades with peoples in many lands far away, \q This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: \q Tyre, you have said, "I am perfectly beautiful."

fr.L: et dis à Tyr, qui habite aux entrées de la mer, \q la marchande des peuples pour des îles nombreuses : \q Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : \q Tyr, tu as dit : « Moi, [je suis] parfaite en beauté. »
fr.B: et dis à Tyr, la ville assise aux portes de la mer, \q qui fait commerce avec les peuples d’îles nombreuses : \q Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : \q Tyr, tu as dit : « Je suis d’une beauté parfaite. »
fr.R: Dis à Tyr, la ville qui garde l’entrée de la mer, \q qui fait du commerce avec les peuples de nombreux pays lointains : \q Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : \q Tyr, tu as dit : « Je suis parfaitement belle. »

decisions.choice: the lament pictures Tyre as a great merchant ship
decisions.reason: The poem tells the story of a ship: how it was built from the finest materials (verses 4-7), crewed and guarded (8-11), loaded with the trade of the whole known world (12-25), and wrecked at sea, while sailors on the shore mourn it (26-36). Tyre, an island city that lived by the sea, is that ship. The chapter is set in lines as poetry from here to verse 36, following the Hebrew accents. The list of trading partners in verses 12-24 reads like a merchant's register and is set in lines too, so that the poem is not broken.

decisions.choice: the entrances of the sea: harbors
decisions.reason: Tyre had harbors on its island, the gates through which the sea trade came in and went out.

decisions.choice: I am perfect in beauty: the boast the lament answers
decisions.reason: Tyre's own words sum up its pride. The same "perfect in beauty" is said of the king of Tyre (28:12) and of Jerusalem, also brought low (Lamentations 2:15; Ezekiel 16:14).

decisions.choice: no quotation marks for the message; double quotation marks for Tyre's boast
decisions.reason: Under the quotation rule for Ezekiel, the message Ezekiel is told to deliver takes no quotation marks, and human speech quoted inside it takes double quotes. "Coastlands" follows the Isaiah table ("lands far away" at Readable).

decisions.choice: the lament over Tyre (27:3b-36) set in lines; Tyre, pictured as a ship, keeps the feminine ("parfaite", "tu as été remplie") at every level
alternatives: masculine agreement for the ship ("le navire")
decisions.reason: The term sheet names Tyre in Ezekiel 27 as a city addressed as a woman; French keeps the city's agreement even where the picture is a ship.

source.text: בְּלֵ֥ב יַמִּ֖ים גְּבוּלָ֑יִךְ בֹּנַ֕יִךְ כָּלְל֖וּ יָפְיֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] heart of [the] seas [are] your borders; your builders perfected your beauty.

en.L: In the heart of the seas [are] your borders; \q your builders made your beauty perfect.
en.B: Your territory is in the heart of the seas; \q your builders made your beauty perfect.
en.R: Your home is far out in the sea. \q Those who built you made you perfectly beautiful.

fr.L: Au cœur des mers [sont] tes frontières ; \q tes bâtisseurs ont rendu parfaite ta beauté.
fr.B: Ton domaine est au cœur des mers ; \q tes bâtisseurs ont rendu ta beauté parfaite.
fr.R: Tu habites loin dans la mer. \q Ceux qui t’ont construite t’ont rendue parfaitement belle.

decisions.choice: the heart of the seas: the open sea
decisions.reason: The phrase means the high seas, far from shore (verses 25-27). It fits both the ship and the island city.

decisions.choice: your builders: the picture becomes a ship
decisions.reason: From here the city is described as a ship that its builders made perfect.

source.text: בְּרוֹשִׁ֤ים מִשְּׂנִיר֙ בָּ֣נוּ לָ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־לֻֽחֹתָ֑יִם אֶ֤רֶז מִלְּבָנוֹן֙ לָקָ֔חוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת תֹּ֖רֶן עָלָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Of] junipers from Senir they built for you all [the] planks; a cedar from Lebanon they took to make a mast on you.

en.L: Of junipers from Senir they built all your planks for you; \q a cedar from Lebanon they took to make a mast for you.
en.B: They built all your planks from the junipers of Senir; \q a cedar from Lebanon was taken to be your mast.
en.R: Your builders used juniper trees from Mount Hermon to make all your boards. \q They took a cedar from Lebanon to make your mast.

fr.L: En genévriers de Senir ils t’ont construit toutes tes planches ; \q un cèdre du Liban, ils l’ont pris pour faire sur toi un mât.
fr.B: Ils ont fait toutes tes planches avec les genévriers de Senir ; \q on a pris un cèdre du Liban pour te faire un mât.
fr.R: Tes constructeurs ont utilisé les genévriers du mont Hermon pour faire toutes tes planches. \q Ils ont pris un cèdre du Liban pour faire ton mât.

decisions.choice: Senir: Mount Hermon
decisions.reason: Senir was the Amorite name of Mount Hermon, north of Israel (Deuteronomy 3:9).

decisions.choice: junipers and a cedar from Lebanon: the finest timber of the region
decisions.reason: The tall conifers of the Lebanon and Hermon ranges were prized for building (1 Kings 5:20-24). A straight cedar made a fine mast.

decisions.choice: Mount Hermon
decisions.reason: Readable gives the familiar name of the mountain. "Junipers" follows Isaiah 14:8.

source.text: אַלּוֹנִים֙ מִבָּ֔שָׁן עָשׂ֖וּ מִשּׁוֹטָ֑יִךְ קַרְשֵׁ֤ךְ עָֽשׂוּ־שֵׁן֙ בַּת־אֲשֻׁרִ֔ים מֵאִיֵּ֖י כִּתִּיִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [Of] oaks from Bashan they made your oars; your deck they made [of] ivory, daughter of Ashurim, from [the] coastlands of Kittim.

en.L: [Of] oaks from Bashan they made your oars; \q your deck they made of ivory [set in] box wood from the coastlands of Kittim.
en.B: They made your oars of oaks from Bashan; \q they made your deck of box wood from the coastlands of Kittim, inlaid with ivory.
en.R: Your oars were made of oak trees from Bashan. \q Your deck was made of box wood from Cyprus and decorated with ivory.

fr.L: [En] chênes du Bashân ils ont fait tes rames ; \q ton pont, ils l’ont fait d’ivoire [serti dans] du buis des îles de Kittim.
fr.B: Ils ont fait tes rames avec les chênes du Bashân ; \q ils ont fait ton pont de buis des îles de Kittim, incrusté d’ivoire.
fr.R: Tes rames étaient faites de chênes du Bashân. \q Ton pont était fait de buis de Chypre et décoré d’ivoire.

decisions.choice: oaks from Bashan: the famous oaks east of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Bashan was known for its oaks and its cattle (Isaiah 2:13; Amos 4:1).

decisions.choice: ivory set in box wood
alternatives: ivory, the work of the Ashurites
decisions.reason: Divided as the Hebrew text has it, the words read "ivory, daughter of the Ashurites". Read as one word, they give the name of a tree, the box tree (Isaiah 41:19; 60:13), and the sense "ivory in box wood". The second reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: Kittim: Cyprus
decisions.reason: Kittim is named after the city of Kition on Cyprus and stands for Cyprus and the islands west of it (Isaiah 23:1, 12).

decisions.choice: Cyprus
decisions.reason: Readable says "Cyprus" for Kittim, as the Isaiah table sets.

decisions.choice: "les îles de Kittim" (L, B); "Chypre" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names table: Kittim (L, B) / Chypre (R), as the English R says Cyprus.

source.text: שֵׁשׁ־בְּרִקְמָ֤ה מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ הָיָ֣ה מִפְרָשֵׂ֔ךְ לִהְי֥וֹת לָ֖ךְ לְנֵ֑ס תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן מֵאִיֵּ֥י אֱלִישָׁ֖ה הָיָ֥ה מְכַסֵּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt was your sail, to be for you a banner; blue and purple from [the] coastlands of Elishah was your covering.

en.L: Fine linen with embroidered work from Egypt was your sail, \q to be your banner; \q blue and purple from the coastlands of Elishah was your awning.
en.B: Your sail was of fine embroidered linen from Egypt, \q and it served as your banner; \q your awning was of blue and purple cloth from the coastlands of Elishah.
en.R: Your sail was made of fine linen from Egypt, with colorful designs. \q It was your flag. \q Your sunshade was made of blue and purple cloth from the coasts of Elishah.

fr.L: Le fin lin brodé d’Égypte était ta voile, \q pour te servir d’étendard ; \q le bleu et la pourpre des îles d’Élisha étaient ton abri.
fr.B: Ta voile était de fin lin brodé d’Égypte, \q et elle te servait d’étendard ; \q ton abri était d’étoffes bleues et pourpres des îles d’Élisha.
fr.R: Ta voile était faite de fin lin d’Égypte, avec des dessins de couleur. \q C’était ton drapeau. \q Ton toit contre le soleil était fait de tissu bleu et pourpre venu des côtes d’Élisha.

decisions.choice: fine linen with embroidery from Egypt
decisions.reason: Egypt was famous for its fine linen (Proverbs 7:16). Such a sail was a luxury.

decisions.choice: a banner: the sail served as the ship's emblem
decisions.reason: The word means a flag or signal. The splendid sail marked the ship from afar.

decisions.choice: blue and purple from Elishah
decisions.reason: Blue and purple dyes were costly; purple was the great product of Phoenicia itself. Elishah is a son of Javan in Genesis 10:4 and probably a land in the west, perhaps on Cyprus.

decisions.choice: sunshade (R); awning (L, B)
decisions.reason: The covering was an awning over the deck. Readable says what it was for.

source.text: יֹשְׁבֵ֤י צִידוֹן֙ וְאַרְוַ֔ד הָי֥וּ שָׁטִ֖ים לָ֑ךְ חֲכָמַ֤יִךְ צוֹר֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ הֵ֖מָּה חֹבְלָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were rowers for you; your skilled [men], Tyre, were in you; they [were] your sailors.

en.L: The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were rowers for you; \q your skilled men, Tyre, were in you; they [were] your sailors.
en.B: Men from Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; \q your own skilled men, Tyre, were on board as your sailors.
en.R: Men from the cities of Sidon and Arvad rowed for you. \q Your own skilled men, Tyre, were the sailors who steered you.

fr.L: Les habitants de Sidon et d’Arvad étaient tes rameurs ; \q tes sages, Tyr, étaient en toi ; eux, [ils étaient] tes matelots.
fr.B: Les hommes de Sidon et d’Arvad étaient tes rameurs ; \q tes propres experts, Tyr, étaient à bord comme matelots.
fr.R: Des hommes des villes de Sidon et d’Arvad ramaient pour toi. \q Tes propres hommes habiles, Tyr, étaient les marins qui te dirigeaient.

decisions.choice: Sidon and Arvad: Phoenician cities north of Tyre
decisions.reason: Sidon, Tyre's older sister city, lay about twenty-five miles to the north (28:21). Arvad was an island city farther north, on the coast of Syria (Genesis 10:18).

decisions.choice: your skilled men were your sailors: Tyre's own men held the skilled posts
decisions.reason: Other cities supplied the rowers; Tyre's own men were the sailors who handled the ship.

decisions.choice: sailors
decisions.reason: The word for the ship's skilled hands (those who handle the ropes) is "sailors" at every level in this chapter, and the more general word in verses 9, 27 and 29 is "mariners" (L, B) or "seamen" (R).

source.text: זִקְנֵ֨י גְבַ֤ל וַחֲכָמֶ֨יהָ֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ מַחֲזִיקֵ֖י בִּדְקֵ֑ךְ כָּל־אֳנִיּ֨וֹת הַיָּ֤ם וּמַלָּֽחֵיהֶם֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ לַעֲרֹ֖ב מַעֲרָבֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] elders of Gebal and its wise [men] were in you, repairing your seams; all [the] ships of the sea and their mariners were in you, to trade your merchandise.

en.L: The elders of Gebal and its wise men were in you, \q repairing your seams; \q all the ships of the sea and their mariners were in you \q to trade your merchandise.
en.B: The veteran craftsmen of Gebal were on board, \q caulking your seams. \q All the ships of the sea and their crews came to you \q to barter for your goods.
en.R: Experienced workers from Gebal were with you. \q They sealed the cracks between your boards. \q All the ships on the sea and their seamen came to you \q to trade for your goods.

fr.L: Les anciens de Guebal et ses sages étaient en toi, \q réparant tes fissures ; \q tous les navires de la mer et leurs marins étaient en toi \q pour échanger tes marchandises.
fr.B: Les artisans chevronnés de Guebal étaient à bord, \q et ils calfataient tes fentes. \q Tous les navires de la mer et leurs équipages venaient chez toi \q pour échanger tes marchandises.
fr.R: Des ouvriers expérimentés de Guebal étaient avec toi. \q Ils bouchaient les fentes entre tes planches. \q Tous les bateaux de la mer et leurs marins venaient chez toi \q pour acheter tes marchandises.

decisions.choice: Gebal: the Phoenician city of Byblos
decisions.reason: Gebal, north of modern Beirut, was known for its skilled builders (1 Kings 5:32; Joshua 13:5).

decisions.choice: the elders and wise men of Gebal: master craftsmen
decisions.reason: Here "elders" and "wise men" are experienced, skilled workers.

decisions.choice: all the ships of the sea came to you
decisions.reason: The picture widens from one ship to the harbor city, where the ships of every nation came to trade.

decisions.choice: "Guebal" at every level
decisions.reason: The form of published 1 Kings 5:32 and of the term sheet; the meaning decision names Byblos.

source.text: פָּרַ֨ס וְל֤וּד וּפוּט֙ הָי֣וּ בְחֵילֵ֔ךְ אַנְשֵׁ֖י מִלְחַמְתֵּ֑ךְ מָגֵ֤ן וְכוֹבַע֙ תִּלּוּ־בָ֔ךְ הֵ֖מָּה נָתְנ֥וּ הֲדָרֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Persia and Lud and Put were in your army, your men of war; shield and helmet they hung in you; they gave your splendor.

en.L: Persia and Lud and Put were in your army, your men of war; \q shield and helmet they hung in you; \q they gave you your splendor.
en.B: Men of Persia, Lud and Put served in your army as your warriors. \q They hung their shields and helmets in you; \q they gave you your splendor.
en.R: Soldiers from Persia, Lud and Put served in your army. \q They hung up their shields and helmets inside you. \q They made you look splendid.

fr.L: La Perse, Lud et Puth étaient dans ton armée, tes hommes de guerre ; \q le bouclier et le casque, ils les suspendaient chez toi ; \q ils te donnaient ta splendeur.
fr.B: Des hommes de Perse, de Lud et de Puth servaient dans ton armée comme guerriers. \q Ils suspendaient chez toi leurs boucliers et leurs casques ; \q ils te donnaient ta splendeur.
fr.R: Des soldats de Perse, de Lud et de Puth servaient dans ton armée. \q Ils accrochaient leurs boucliers et leurs casques chez toi. \q Grâce à eux, tu étais magnifique.

decisions.choice: Persia, Lud and Put: hired soldiers from distant lands
decisions.reason: Tyre hired soldiers from far away. Put is Libya in north Africa (30:5; Jeremiah 46:9). Lud may be Lydia in Asia Minor or a people of Africa (Genesis 10:13; Isaiah 66:19). Persia was still a small land east of Babylon in Ezekiel's day; it is named again with Cush and Put in 38:5.

decisions.choice: shield and helmet hung in you: weapons on display
decisions.reason: Soldiers hung their shields on walls and towers as a show of strength (Song of Songs 4:4).

source.text: בְּנֵ֧י אַרְוַ֣ד וְחֵילֵ֗ךְ עַל־חוֹמוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ סָבִ֔יב וְגַ֨מָּדִ֔ים בְּמִגְדְּלוֹתַ֖יִךְ הָי֑וּ שִׁלְטֵיהֶ֞ם תִּלּ֤וּ עַל־חוֹמוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ סָבִ֔יב הֵ֖מָּה כָּלְל֥וּ יָפְיֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Arvad and Helech [were] on your walls all around, and Gammadites in your towers were; their shields they hung on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.

en.L: The sons of Arvad and Helech [were] on your walls all around, \q and Gammadites were in your towers; \q their shields they hung on your walls all around; \q they made your beauty perfect.
en.B: Men of Arvad and Helech manned your walls on every side, \q and men of Gamad were in your towers. \q Their shields hung around your walls; \q they made your beauty perfect.
en.R: Soldiers from Arvad and Helech stood guard all around your walls. \q Men from Gamad were in your towers. \q They hung their shields all around your walls. \q They made you perfectly beautiful.

fr.L: Les fils d’Arvad et Hélek [étaient] sur tes murailles tout autour, \q et des Gammadiens étaient dans tes tours ; \q leurs boucliers, ils les suspendaient à tes murailles tout autour ; \q ils ont rendu parfaite ta beauté.
fr.B: Les hommes d’Arvad et de Hélek gardaient tes murailles tout autour, \q et les hommes de Gamad étaient dans tes tours. \q Leurs boucliers étaient suspendus tout autour de tes murailles ; \q ils ont rendu ta beauté parfaite.
fr.R: Des soldats d’Arvad et de Hélek montaient la garde tout autour de tes murailles. \q Des hommes de Gamad étaient dans tes tours. \q Ils accrochaient leurs boucliers tout autour de tes murailles. \q Ils t’ont rendue parfaitement belle.

decisions.choice: Helech: a place, or "your army"
decisions.reason: The word may be a place name, perhaps Cilicia in southern Asia Minor, or the word "your army" from verse 10.

decisions.choice: Gammadites: an unknown people
decisions.reason: The name occurs only here. Who they were is not known.

decisions.choice: they made your beauty perfect: the words of verse 4
decisions.reason: The description of the ship and its guard ends where it began.

decisions.choice: Men of Arvad (B); Soldiers from Arvad (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the sons of Arvad"; the guards on the walls were soldiers, so Balanced and Readable say "men" and "soldiers".

source.text: תַּרְשִׁ֥ישׁ סֹחַרְתֵּ֖ךְ מֵרֹ֣ב כָּל־ה֑וֹן בְּכֶ֤סֶף בַּרְזֶל֙ בְּדִ֣יל וְעוֹפֶ֔רֶת נָתְנ֖וּ עִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Tarshish [was] your trader from [the] abundance of all wealth; for silver, iron, tin and lead they gave your wares.

en.L: Tarshish [was] your trader because of the abundance of all [kinds of] wealth; \q with silver, iron, tin and lead they paid for your wares.
en.B: Tarshish did business with you because of your great wealth of every kind; \q they traded silver, iron, tin and lead for your goods.
en.R: The people of Tarshish traded with you because you had so many good things to sell. \q They gave you silver, iron, tin and lead in exchange for your goods.

fr.L: Tarsis [était] ta marchande à cause de l’abondance de toute richesse ; \q avec de l’argent, du fer, de l’étain et du plomb, ils payaient tes produits.
fr.B: Tarsis faisait commerce avec toi à cause de tes richesses de toute sorte ; \q on t’échangeait de l’argent, du fer, de l’étain et du plomb contre tes produits.
fr.R: Les gens de Tarsis faisaient du commerce avec toi, parce que tu avais beaucoup de bonnes choses à vendre. \q Ils te donnaient de l’argent, du fer, de l’étain et du plomb en échange de tes produits.

decisions.choice: verses 12-24: Tyre's trading partners
decisions.reason: The list names Tyre's partners in trade and what each supplied, from the far west to Asia Minor, the north, Arabia and Mesopotamia. Several names and goods are rare or unknown, and decisions say where.

decisions.choice: Tarshish: a port in the far west
decisions.reason: Tarshish lay far to the west across the Mediterranean (Jonah 1:3). It is often placed in southern Spain, rich in metals.

decisions.choice: your wares: goods left in exchange
decisions.reason: The word for "wares" is found only in this chapter. It seems to mean goods given or left in exchange.

decisions.choice: the trading partners of 12-24 keep their published French names: "Tarsis", "Javan" (L, B; "la Grèce" at R), "Tubal", "Méshek", "Beth-Togarma", "Dedan", "Saba", "Raama", "Harân", "Assour"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names table and the published Genesis 10 and 1 Chronicles 1.

en.B: Javan, Tubal and Meshech traded with you; \q they exchanged slaves and bronze vessels for your goods.
en.R: The people of Greece, Tubal and Meshech traded with you. \q They sold you slaves and things made of bronze in exchange for your goods.

fr.R: Les gens de la Grèce, de Tubal et de Méshek faisaient du commerce avec toi. \q Ils te vendaient des esclaves et des objets en bronze en échange de tes marchandises.

decisions.choice: Javan, Tubal and Meshech: the Greeks and peoples of Asia Minor
decisions.reason: Javan is Ionia, the Greeks of the Aegean coasts and islands (Genesis 10:2; Daniel 8:21). Tubal and Meshech were peoples of central and eastern Asia Minor (32:26; 38:2).

decisions.choice: the lives of human beings: slaves
decisions.reason: People were bought and sold. Joel 4:6 accuses Tyre and Sidon of selling the people of Judah to the Greeks, and Amos 1:9 condemns Tyre's slave trade.

decisions.choice: slaves (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the lives of human beings". Balanced and Readable say "slaves", since people sold as property are meant, under the style guide's rule for slavery.

decisions.choice: Greece
decisions.reason: Readable says "Greece" for Javan here, as the name is used in Daniel 8:21.

fr.R: Des gens de Beth-Togarma \q t’échangeaient des chevaux, des chevaux de guerre et des mulets contre tes produits.

decisions.choice: Beth-togarmah: a land of horses in eastern Asia Minor
decisions.reason: Togarmah is a son of Gomer (Genesis 10:3) and is placed in the far north (38:6), perhaps in the region of Armenia.

decisions.choice: steeds: riding or war horses
decisions.reason: The word usually means horsemen, but beside "horses" and "mules" it means horses for riding or for war.

source.text: בְּנֵ֤י דְדָן֙ רֹֽכְלַ֔יִךְ אִיִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים סְחֹרַ֣ת יָדֵ֑ךְ קַרְנ֥וֹת שֵׁן֙ וְהָבְנִ֔ים הֵשִׁ֖יבוּ אֶשְׁכָּרֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Dedan [were] your traders; many coastlands [were the] market of your hand; horns of ivory and ebony they brought back [as] your payment.

en.L: The sons of Dedan [were] your traders; \q many coastlands [were] the market of your hand; \q horns of ivory and ebony they brought back [as] your payment.
en.B: The people of Dedan traded with you; \q many coastlands were markets under your control; \q they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
en.R: The people of Dedan traded with you. \q Many lands across the sea bought your goods. \q They paid you with elephant tusks and ebony wood.

fr.L: Les fils de Dedan [étaient] tes marchands ; \q des îles nombreuses [étaient] le marché de ta main ; \q des cornes d’ivoire et de l’ébène, ils te [les] rapportaient [en] paiement.

decisions.choice: the sons of Dedan
decisions.reason: Dedan, an Arabian people, comes again in verse 20. The Greek translation reads "Rhodes" here (stated from general knowledge); the Hebrew letters for d and r look much alike, and Rhodes would fit the "coastlands" that follow. The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: the market of your hand: markets under your control
decisions.reason: The phrase seems to mean that many coastlands traded at Tyre's direction, as its agents or customers.

decisions.choice: horns of ivory and ebony: luxuries from far away
decisions.reason: Elephant tusks and black ebony wood came from Africa or India by long trade routes.

source.text: אֲרָ֥ם סֹחַרְתֵּ֖ךְ מֵרֹ֣ב מַעֲשָׂ֑יִךְ בְּ֠נֹפֶךְ אַרְגָּמָ֨ן וְרִקְמָ֤ה וּבוּץ֙ וְרָאמֹ֣ת וְכַדְכֹּ֔ד נָתְנ֖וּ בְּעִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

en.L: Aram [was] your trader because of the abundance of your products; \q with turquoise, purple and embroidered work, and fine linen and coral and rubies they paid for your wares.
en.B: Aram did business with you because you had so many products; \q they gave turquoise, purple cloth, embroidered work, fine linen, coral and rubies for your goods.
en.R: The people of Aram traded with you because you made so many things. \q They gave you turquoise, purple cloth, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral and rubies for your goods.

fr.R: Les gens d’Aram faisaient du commerce avec toi, parce que tu fabriquais beaucoup de choses. \q Ils te donnaient des turquoises, du tissu pourpre, des broderies, du fin lin, du corail et des rubis en échange de tes produits.

decisions.choice: Aram
decisions.reason: Many Hebrew manuscripts read "Edom", which differs from "Aram" by one similar letter (stated from general knowledge). Edom would fit the gems, and Aram's chief city, Damascus, is named separately in verse 18. The standard text is kept.

decisions.choice: turquoise, coral and rubies: precious stones whose names are uncertain
decisions.reason: The names of gems in Hebrew are hard to identify. The first may be turquoise or emerald (28:13; Exodus 28:18), the second coral (Job 28:18), the third ruby or agate (Isaiah 54:12).

source.text: יְהוּדָה֙ וְאֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֵ֖מָּה רֹכְלָ֑יִךְ בְּחִטֵּ֣י מִ֠נִּית וּפַנַּ֨ג וּדְבַ֤שׁ וָשֶׁ֨מֶן֙ וָצֹ֔רִי נָתְנ֖וּ מַעֲרָבֵֽךְ׃

en.B: Judah and the land of Israel were your traders; \q for your goods they gave wheat from Minnith, millet, honey, oil and balm.
en.R: The people of Judah and Israel traded with you. \q They gave you wheat from Minnith, millet, honey, olive oil and balm for your goods.

decisions.choice: Judah and the land of Israel among Tyre's partners
decisions.reason: Israel had long supplied Tyre with farm produce in exchange for timber and skill (1 Kings 5:25; Acts 12:20). God's people too were part of Tyre's world of trade.

decisions.choice: Minnith: a town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Minnith is named in Judges 11:33, in the land of Ammon. The wheat may have come from there or been named for it.

decisions.choice: pannag: an unknown food
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It may be a kind of millet, a pastry, or some other foodstuff. Literal keeps the Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: balm: a healing resin
decisions.reason: Balm was a famous product of Gilead (Genesis 37:25; Jeremiah 8:22).

decisions.choice: millet (B, R); pannag (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give a likely sense of the unknown word (m3); Readable says "olive oil" for "oil".

decisions.choice: "pannag" (L), "millet" (B, R), as the English
decisions.reason: The word is unknown (footnoted in the meaning decision); French follows the English levels until the founder rules on the open question.

en.L: Damascus [was] your trader in the abundance of your products, from the abundance of all wealth, \q with wine of Helbon and wool of Zahar.
en.B: Damascus did business with you because of your many products and your great wealth of every kind, \q trading wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
en.R: Damascus traded with you because you had so many products and riches. \q It traded wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.

fr.R: Damas faisait du commerce avec toi, parce que tu avais beaucoup de produits et de richesses. \q Elle t’échangeait du vin de Helbôn et de la laine de Tsahar.

decisions.choice: Damascus and Helbon
decisions.reason: Damascus was the chief city of Aram. Helbon, a village in the hills north of Damascus, was famous for its wine (stated from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: Zahar: a place, or "white" wool
decisions.reason: The word may be a place name or may describe the wool as white.

source.text: וְדָ֤ן וְיָוָן֙ מְאוּזָּ֔ל בְּעִזְבוֹנַ֖יִךְ נָתָ֑נּוּ בַּרְזֶ֤ל עָשׁוֹת֙ קִדָּ֣ה וְקָנֶ֔ה בְּמַעֲרָבֵ֖ךְ הָיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Vedan and Javan from Uzal for your wares gave; iron wrought, cassia and calamus for your merchandise were.

en.L: Vedan and Javan from Uzal gave [goods] for your wares; \q wrought iron, cassia and calamus were [among] your merchandise.
en.B: Vedan and Javan from Uzal traded for your goods; \q wrought iron, cassia and sweet cane were among the goods you bought.
en.R: Vedan and Javan from Uzal traded with you for your goods. \q They brought you iron goods and spices, cassia and sweet cane.

fr.L: Wedân et Javan, depuis Uzal, donnaient [des marchandises] pour tes produits ; \q le fer forgé, la casse et le roseau odorant étaient [parmi] tes marchandises.
fr.B: Wedân et Javan, depuis Uzal, faisaient des échanges pour tes produits ; \q le fer forgé, la casse et le roseau odorant étaient parmi les marchandises que tu achetais.
fr.R: Wedân et Javan, depuis Uzal, faisaient du commerce avec toi pour avoir tes produits. \q Ils t’apportaient des objets en fer et des épices, de la casse et du roseau odorant.

decisions.choice: Vedan and Javan from Uzal: an obscure line
alternatives: and casks of wine from Uzal
decisions.reason: The first word may be a place or may be read "and Dan". This Javan is probably not Greece (verse 13) but a place in Arabia, and Uzal is an Arabian name (Genesis 10:27). Another way of dividing the words gives "and casks of wine from Uzal". No reading is certain, and the names are kept as they stand.

decisions.choice: cassia and calamus: fragrant spices
decisions.reason: Both were used in the holy anointing oil (Exodus 30:23-24). Calamus is a sweet-smelling cane.

decisions.choice: Javan (R)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "Javan" here, since it is not the Greek Javan of verse 13 (m1).

decisions.choice: "Wedân et Javan, depuis Uzal", the English line in French spelling; Javan kept at R as the English R keeps it
decisions.reason: An obscure line (footnoted in the meaning decision); "Uzal" as published 1 Chronicles 1:21.

source.text: דְּדָן֙ רֹֽכַלְתֵּ֔ךְ בְבִגְדֵי־חֹ֖פֶשׁ לְרִכְבָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Dedan [was] your trader in garments of spreading for riding.

en.L: Dedan [was] your trader \q in garments of spread cloth for riding.
en.B: Dedan traded with you \q in saddle blankets for riding.
en.R: The people of Dedan traded with you. \q They sold you saddle blankets.

fr.L: Dedan [était] ta marchande \q en étoffes à étendre pour monter à cheval.
fr.B: Dedan faisait commerce avec toi \q en couvertures de selle.
fr.R: Les gens de Dedan faisaient du commerce avec toi. \q Ils te vendaient des couvertures pour les selles.

decisions.choice: Dedan: an Arabian trading people
decisions.reason: See 25:13. Dedan lay on the caravan routes of northwest Arabia.

decisions.choice: garments of spread cloth for riding: saddlecloths
decisions.reason: The cloths were spread on horses or camels for riding.

source.text: עֲרַב֙ וְכָל־נְשִׂיאֵ֣י קֵדָ֔ר הֵ֖מָּה סֹחֲרֵ֣י יָדֵ֑ךְ בְּכָרִ֤ים וְאֵילִים֙ וְעַתּוּדִ֔ים בָּ֖ם סֹחֲרָֽיִךְ׃

en.L: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar, \q they [were] traders of your hand; \q in lambs and rams and goats, \q in these [they were] your traders.
en.B: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar \q were traders under your hand; \q in lambs, rams and goats, \q in these they did business with you.
en.R: The Arabs and all the rulers of Kedar \q traded with you. \q They brought lambs, rams and goats \q to trade with you.

decisions.choice: Arabia and Kedar: the desert tribes
decisions.reason: Arabia here means the tribes of the desert, and Kedar the Arab tribes descended from Ishmael who lived with their flocks (Isaiah 21:16-17; Jeremiah 49:28).

decisions.choice: princes (L, B); rulers (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *nasi'* in Ezekiel.

source.text: רֹכְלֵ֤י שְׁבָא֙ וְרַעְמָ֔ה הֵ֖מָּה רֹכְלָ֑יִךְ בְּרֹ֨אשׁ כָּל־בֹּ֜שֶׂם וּבְכָל־אֶ֤בֶן יְקָרָה֙ וְזָהָ֔ב נָתְנ֖וּ עִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] traders of Sheba and Raamah, they [were] your traders; with [the] best of every spice and with every precious stone and gold they gave your wares.

en.L: The traders of Sheba and Raamah, they [were] your traders; \q with the best of all spices and with all precious stones and gold they paid for your wares.
en.B: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; \q they gave the finest of all spices, every kind of precious stone, and gold for your goods.
en.R: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah traded with you. \q They gave you the best spices, all kinds of jewels, and gold for your goods.

fr.R: Des marchands de Saba et de Raama faisaient du commerce avec toi. \q Ils te donnaient les meilleurs aromates, toutes sortes de pierres précieuses et de l’or en échange de tes produits.

decisions.choice: Sheba and Raamah: peoples of southern Arabia
decisions.reason: Sheba, in the southwest of Arabia, grew rich on spices, incense, gold and gems (1 Kings 10:1-2, 10). Raamah is named with Sheba in Genesis 10:7.

source.text: חָרָ֤ן וְכַנֵּה֙ וָעֶ֔דֶן רֹכְלֵ֖י שְׁבָ֑א אַשּׁ֖וּר כִּלְמַ֥ד רֹכַלְתֵּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Haran and Canneh and Eden, [the] traders of Sheba, Asshur, Chilmad [was] your trader.

en.L: Haran and Canneh and Eden, the traders of Sheba, \q Asshur [and] Chilmad [was] your trader.
en.B: Haran, Canneh and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, \q Asshur and Chilmad traded with you.
en.R: Haran, Canneh and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, \q Asshur and Chilmad traded with you.

fr.L: Harân, Canné et Éden, les marchands de Saba, \q Assour [et] Kilmad [étaient] ta marchande.
fr.B: Harân, Canné et Éden, les marchands de Saba, \q Assour et Kilmad faisaient commerce avec toi.
fr.R: Harân, Canné et Éden, les marchands de Saba, \q Assour et Kilmad faisaient du commerce avec toi.

decisions.choice: Haran, Canneh, Eden, Asshur and Chilmad: towns of Mesopotamia
decisions.reason: Haran, where Abraham once lived (Genesis 11:31), and Eden (Beth-eden, Amos 1:5; 2 Kings 19:12) were in northern Mesopotamia. Asshur is Assyria or its old capital. Canneh and Chilmad are not known for certain. This Eden is not the garden of Genesis 2.

decisions.choice: the traders of Sheba: out of place in a list of northern towns
decisions.reason: Sheba was named in verse 22 among the Arabian peoples. Here the words may mean merchants from Sheba who traded in the north, or may repeat verse 22.

source.text: הֵ֤מָּה רֹכְלַ֨יִךְ֙ בְּמַכְלֻלִ֔ים בִּגְלוֹמֵי֙ תְּכֵ֣לֶת וְרִקְמָ֔ה וּבְגִנְזֵ֖י בְּרֹמִ֑ים בַּחֲבָלִ֧ים חֲבֻשִׁ֛ים וַאֲרֻזִ֖ים בְּמַרְכֻלְתֵּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: They [were] your traders in choice garments, in cloaks of blue and embroidery, and in carpets of many colors, with cords bound and made firm, in your marketplace.

en.L: They [were] your traders in choice garments, \q in cloaks of blue and embroidered work, and in carpets of many colors, \q with cords twisted and made firm, in your marketplace.
en.B: They traded with you in fine clothing, \q in cloaks of blue and embroidered work, and in multicolored carpets \q tied with cords and well made, in your market.
en.R: They sold you fine clothes, \q blue cloaks and embroidered cloth, and colorful rugs \q tied with strong, twisted cords. They sold them in your market.

fr.L: Eux [étaient] tes marchands en vêtements de choix, \q en manteaux de pourpre bleue et de broderie, et en tapis de plusieurs couleurs, \q avec des cordes tressées et solides, sur ton marché.
fr.B: Ils faisaient commerce avec toi en beaux vêtements, \q en manteaux bleus et brodés, et en tapis multicolores \q liés de cordes et bien faits, sur ton marché.
fr.R: Ils te vendaient de beaux vêtements, \q des manteaux bleus et des tissus brodés, et des tapis de toutes les couleurs \q attachés avec des cordes solides et tressées. Ils les vendaient sur ton marché.

decisions.choice: choice garments, cloaks and carpets: rare words for fine textiles
decisions.reason: Several words here occur only in this verse, and their sense is uncertain. The "carpets" may instead be chests for storing cloth, and "made firm" may describe the cords or the goods.

source.text: אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֔ישׁ שָׁרוֹתַ֖יִךְ מַעֲרָבֵ֑ךְ וַתִּמָּלְאִ֧י וַֽתִּכְבְּדִ֛י מְאֹ֖ד בְּלֵ֥ב־יַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] ships of Tarshish [were] your travelers [for] your merchandise; and you were filled and you were made heavy greatly in [the] heart of [the] seas.

en.L: The ships of Tarshish [were] your caravans [for] your merchandise; \q and you were filled and made very heavy in the heart of the seas.
en.B: Ships of Tarshish carried your goods; \q you were filled with cargo and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.
en.R: Great trading ships carried your goods. \q You were loaded full, a heavy ship far out at sea.

fr.L: Les navires de Tarsis [étaient] tes caravanes [pour] tes marchandises ; \q et tu as été remplie et très alourdie au cœur des mers.
fr.B: Les navires de Tarsis transportaient tes marchandises ; \q tu étais remplie de cargaisons et lourdement chargée au cœur des mers.
fr.R: De grands navires de commerce transportaient tes marchandises. \q Tu étais chargée à ras bord, un lourd navire loin au milieu de la mer.

decisions.choice: ships of Tarshish: great seagoing trading ships
decisions.reason: The name of the distant port Tarshish was given to the large ships built for long voyages (Isaiah 2:16; 23:1).

decisions.choice: made very heavy: richly laden, and also honored
decisions.reason: The verb means "be heavy" and also "be honored, glorious". The ship is weighed down with cargo, and the city with glory, and in verse 26 the heavy ship goes down.

decisions.choice: great trading ships
decisions.reason: Readable follows the Isaiah table for "ships of Tarshish".

decisions.choice: "les navires de Tarsis" (L, B); "de grands navires de commerce" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled French wording of the term in Isaiah and 1 Kings 10:22.

source.text: בְּמַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ הֱבִיא֔וּךְ הַשָּׁטִ֖ים אֹתָ֑ךְ ר֚וּחַ הַקָּדִ֔ים שְׁבָרֵ֖ךְ בְּלֵ֥ב יַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Into waters many they have brought you, those rowing you; the wind of the east has broken you in [the] heart of [the] seas.

en.L: Into many waters your rowers have brought you; \q the wind of the east has shattered you in the heart of the seas.
en.B: Your rowers brought you out onto the mighty waters; \q the east wind wrecked you in the heart of the seas.
en.R: The men who rowed you took you out into deep water. \q But the east wind wrecked you far out at sea.

fr.L: En de grandes eaux t’ont amenée ceux qui te font ramer ; \q le vent d’orient t’a brisée au cœur des mers.
fr.B: Tes rameurs t’ont menée sur les eaux puissantes ; \q le vent d’est t’a brisée au cœur des mers.
fr.R: Les hommes qui ramaient pour toi t’ont emmenée en eau profonde. \q Mais le vent d’est t’a brisée loin au milieu de la mer.

decisions.choice: the east wind: a violent storm wind
decisions.reason: The east wind could wreck ships (Psalm 48:8, where it shatters ships of Tarshish). In 17:10 and 19:12 it pictures Babylon.

decisions.choice: the turn of the poem
decisions.reason: The ship is now at sea, far from shore, and the storm breaks it. The lament moves from glory to wreck.

source.text: הוֹנֵךְ֙ וְעִזְבוֹנַ֔יִךְ מַעֲרָבֵ֕ךְ מַלָּחַ֖יִךְ וְחֹבְלָ֑יִךְ מַחֲזִיקֵ֣י בִדְקֵ֣ךוְֽעֹרְבֵ֣י מַ֠עֲרָבֵךְ וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִלְחַמְתֵּ֜ךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֗ךְ וּבְכָל־קְהָלֵךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹכֵ֔ךְ יִפְּלוּ֙ בְּלֵ֣ב יַמִּ֔ים בְּי֖וֹם מַפַּלְתֵּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your wealth and your wares, your merchandise, your mariners and your sailors, those repairing your seams and those trading your merchandise, and all your men of war who [are] in you, and with all your company which [is] in your midst, will fall in [the] heart of [the] seas on [the] day of your downfall.

en.L: Your wealth and your wares, your merchandise, \q your mariners and your sailors, \q those who repair your seams and those who trade your merchandise, and all your fighting men who [are] in you, and all your company that [is] in your midst, \q will fall into the heart of the seas \q on the day of your downfall.
en.B: Your wealth, your wares and your goods, \q your mariners and your sailors, \q those who caulk your seams and those who trade your goods, all your warriors on board and all the crew within you, \q will sink into the heart of the seas \q on the day of your downfall.
en.R: Your riches, your goods and everything you trade, \q your seamen and your sailors, \q the workers who fix your leaks, your merchants, your soldiers and everyone else on board \q will sink to the bottom of the sea \q on the day you are wrecked.

fr.L: Tes richesses et tes produits, tes marchandises, \q tes marins et tes matelots, \q ceux qui réparent tes fissures et ceux qui échangent tes marchandises, et tous tes hommes de guerre qui [sont] en toi, et toute ta foule qui [est] au milieu de toi, \q tomberont au cœur des mers \q au jour de ta chute.
fr.B: Tes richesses, tes produits et tes marchandises, \q tes marins et tes matelots, \q ceux qui calfatent tes fentes et ceux qui échangent tes marchandises, tous tes guerriers à bord et tout l’équipage qui est en toi, \q sombreront au cœur des mers \q au jour de ton naufrage.
fr.R: Tes richesses, tes produits et tout ce que tu vends, \q tes marins et tes matelots, \q les ouvriers qui réparent tes fuites, tes marchands, tes soldats et tous les autres à bord \q couleront au fond de la mer \q le jour où tu feras naufrage.

decisions.choice: everything named in the poem goes down with the ship
decisions.reason: The list gathers the cargo, the crew, the craftsmen and the soldiers of verses 8-24. All of it sinks together.

decisions.choice: will fall: will sink
decisions.reason: The verb "fall" here is used of going down into the sea.

source.text: לְק֖וֹל זַעֲקַ֣ת חֹבְלָ֑יִךְ יִרְעֲשׁ֖וּ מִגְרֹשֽׁוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: At [the] sound of [the] cry of your sailors will shake [the] pasturelands.

en.L: At the sound of the cry of your sailors \q the pasturelands will shake.
en.B: At the sound of your sailors' cry \q the shores will quake.
en.R: When your sailors cry out, \q the people on the shore will shake with fear.

fr.L: Au bruit du cri de tes matelots \q les pâturages trembleront.
fr.B: Au bruit des cris de tes matelots, \q les rivages trembleront.
fr.R: Quand tes matelots crieront, \q les gens sur le rivage trembleront de peur.

decisions.choice: the pasturelands: the open land along the shore
decisions.reason: The word usually means the open land around a town. Here it seems to be the coastland near Tyre, which shakes at the cry from the wreck.

decisions.choice: the shores (B); the people on the shore (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which land is meant (m1).

source.text: וְֽיָרְד֞וּ מֵאָנִיּֽוֹתֵיהֶ֗םכֹּ֚ל תֹּפְשֵׂ֣י מָשׁ֔וֹט מַלָּחִ֕ים כֹּ֖ל חֹבְלֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם אֶל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יַעֲמֹֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will come down from their ships, all handling an oar, mariners, all [the] sailors of the sea; on the land they will stand.

en.L: And they will come down from their ships, all who handle the oar, \q mariners, all the sailors of the sea; \q on the land they will stand.
en.B: All who handle the oar will come down from their ships, \q the mariners and all the sailors of the sea; \q they will stand on the shore.
en.R: All the men who row ships will leave them. \q The seamen and all the sailors on the sea \q will stand on the shore.

fr.L: Et ils descendront de leurs navires, tous ceux qui manient la rame, \q les marins, tous les matelots de la mer ; \q sur la terre ils se tiendront.
fr.B: Tous ceux qui manient la rame descendront de leurs navires, \q les marins et tous les matelots de la mer ; \q ils se tiendront sur le rivage.
fr.R: Tous les hommes qui rament sur les bateaux les quitteront. \q Les marins et tous les matelots de la mer \q se tiendront sur le rivage.

decisions.choice: the crews of other ships come ashore to mourn
decisions.reason: The seafarers of every ship leave their own vessels and stand on land to mourn the great ship that has sunk.

source.text: וְהִשְׁמִ֤יעוּ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ בְּקוֹלָ֔ם וְיִזְעֲק֖וּ מָרָ֑ה וְיַעֲל֤וּ עָֽפָר֙ עַל־רָ֣אשֵׁיהֶ֔ם בָּאֵ֖פֶר יִתְפַּלָּֽשׁוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will make heard over you with their voice, and they will cry out bitterly, and they will bring up dust on their heads; in ashes they will roll.

en.L: And they will make their voice heard over you and cry out bitterly, \q and they will throw dust on their heads; \q in ashes they will roll.
en.B: They will raise their voices over you and cry out bitterly. \q They will heap dust on their heads \q and wallow in ashes.
en.R: They will cry out loudly and bitterly about you. \q They will throw dust on their heads \q and roll in ashes.

fr.L: Et ils feront entendre leur voix sur toi et crieront amèrement, \q et ils jetteront de la poussière sur leurs têtes ; \q dans la cendre ils se rouleront.
fr.B: Ils élèveront la voix sur toi et pousseront des cris amers. \q Ils se jetteront de la poussière sur la tête \q et se rouleront dans la cendre.
fr.R: Ils pleureront sur toi avec de grands cris pleins d’amertume. \q Ils se jetteront de la poussière sur la tête \q et se rouleront dans la cendre.

decisions.choice: dust on the head, rolling in ashes: signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Mourners threw dust on their heads and rolled in the dust or ashes (Joshua 7:6; Jeremiah 6:26; Micah 1:10).

source.text: וְהִקְרִ֤יחוּ אֵלַ֨יִךְ֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְחָגְר֖וּ שַׂקִּ֑ים וּבָכ֥וּ אֵלַ֛יִךְ בְּמַר־נֶ֖פֶשׁ מִסְפֵּ֥ד מָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will make bald for you baldness, and they will gird on sackcloths, and they will weep over you in bitterness of soul, [with] wailing bitter.

en.L: And they will make themselves bald for you and gird on sackcloth, \q and they will weep over you in bitterness of soul, [with] bitter wailing.
en.B: They will shave their heads because of you and put on sackcloth. \q They will weep over you with anguish of heart and bitter wailing.
en.R: They will shave their heads because of you and wear rough sackcloth. \q They will cry for you with broken hearts and mourn bitterly.

fr.L: Et ils se raseront la tête à cause de toi et se ceindront de sacs, \q et ils pleureront sur toi dans l’amertume de l’âme, [avec] une lamentation amère.
fr.B: Ils se raseront la tête à cause de toi et revêtiront des sacs. \q Ils pleureront sur toi, le cœur plein d’angoisse, avec des lamentations amères.
fr.R: Ils se raseront la tête à cause de toi et mettront des vêtements de deuil. \q Ils pleureront sur toi, le cœur brisé, et se lamenteront amèrement.

decisions.choice: shaved heads and sackcloth: the dress of mourning
decisions.reason: Mourners shaved their heads and wore sackcloth, a rough cloth of goat hair (7:18; Isaiah 15:2-3; Amos 8:10).

decisions.choice: anguish of heart
decisions.reason: Balanced says "heart" for *nefesh*, the inner self, as in 25:6.

source.text: וְנָשְׂא֨וּ אֵלַ֤יִךְ בְּנִיהֶם֙ קִינָ֔ה וְקוֹנְנ֖וּ עָלָ֑יִךְ מִ֣י כְצ֔וֹר כְּדֻמָ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will take up for you in their wailing a lament, and they will lament over you: Who [is] like Tyre, like one silenced in [the] midst of the sea?

en.L: And they will raise a lament for you in their wailing, and lament over you: \q "Who [is] like Tyre, \q like one silenced in the midst of the sea?
en.B: As they wail, they will raise a lament over you and chant over you: \q "Who was ever like Tyre, \q now silent in the middle of the sea?
en.R: As they cry, they will sing a funeral song about you: \q "Was there ever a city like Tyre? \q Now it lies silent in the middle of the sea!

fr.L: Et ils entonneront sur toi, dans leurs lamentations, une complainte, et ils se lamenteront sur toi : \q « Qui [est] comme Tyr, \q comme celle qui est réduite au silence au milieu de la mer ?
fr.B: En gémissant, ils entonneront une complainte sur toi et ils chanteront sur toi : \q « Qui fut jamais comme Tyr, \q maintenant silencieuse au milieu de la mer ?
fr.R: En pleurant, ils chanteront sur toi un chant de deuil : \q « Y a-t-il jamais eu une ville comme Tyr ? \q Maintenant elle est silencieuse au milieu de la mer !

decisions.choice: the sailors' lament: from here to the end of verse 36
alternatives: the sailors' lament is verse 32 alone
decisions.reason: The seafarers sing their own lament inside Ezekiel's. It probably runs to the end of the chapter, which speaks to Tyre as "you" and closes on the refrain of 26:21; it may instead end with this verse. The quotation marks are placed to verse 36.

decisions.choice: like one silenced: brought to silence, destroyed
decisions.reason: The word is unusual. It probably means silenced, as the dead are silent; with a change of a letter it could mean "like a fortress" or "like a ruin".

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the sailors' lament
decisions.reason: Their words are human speech quoted inside the lament Ezekiel is given, so they take double quotes. Readable turns the question into an exclamation of grief in its second line.

source.text: בְּצֵ֤את עִזְבוֹנַ֨יִךְ֙ מִיַּמִּ֔ים הִשְׂבַּ֖עַתְּ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים בְּרֹ֤ב הוֹנַ֨יִךְ֙ וּמַ֣עֲרָבַ֔יִךְ הֶעֱשַׁ֖רְתְּ מַלְכֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: When went out your wares from [the] seas, you satisfied many peoples; with [the] abundance of your riches and your merchandise you made rich [the] kings of [the] earth.

en.L: When your wares went out from the seas, \q you satisfied many peoples; \q with the abundance of your riches and your merchandise \q you enriched the kings of the earth.
en.B: When your goods went out across the seas, \q you satisfied many peoples; \q with your great wealth and your merchandise \q you made the kings of the earth rich.
en.R: When your goods went out across the seas, \q you supplied what many nations needed. \q Your great riches and the goods you traded \q made the kings of the earth rich.

fr.L: Quand tes produits sortaient des mers, \q tu rassasiais des peuples nombreux ; \q par l’abondance de tes richesses et de tes marchandises \q tu enrichissais les rois de la terre.
fr.B: Quand tes marchandises partaient au-delà des mers, \q tu rassasiais des peuples nombreux ; \q par l’abondance de tes richesses et de tes marchandises, \q tu enrichissais les rois de la terre.
fr.R: Quand tes marchandises partaient au-delà des mers, \q tu donnais à beaucoup de nations ce dont elles avaient besoin. \q Tes grandes richesses et les produits que tu vendais \q rendaient riches les rois de la terre.

decisions.choice: the kings and merchants of the earth: echoed in Revelation 18
decisions.reason: Revelation 18:3, 9-19 takes up this chapter in its lament over Babylon: the kings and merchants of the earth who grew rich from her trade, the seafarers who stand far off and throw dust on their heads, and the cry "What city was like the great city?"

source.text: עֵ֛ת נִשְׁבֶּ֥רֶת מִיַּמִּ֖ים בְּמַֽעֲמַקֵּי־מָ֑יִם מַעֲרָבֵ֥ךְ וְכָל־קְהָלֵ֖ךְ בְּתוֹכֵ֥ךְ נָפָֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] time [of] being broken by [the] seas in [the] depths of [the] waters, your merchandise and all your company in your midst have fallen.

en.L: [At the] time [you are] shattered by the seas, in the deep places of the waters, \q your merchandise and all your company in your midst have fallen.
en.B: Now that you are wrecked by the seas, in the depths of the waters, \q your goods and all your crew have sunk with you.
en.R: Now the sea has wrecked you, and you lie deep under the water. \q Your goods and all your crew have gone down with you.

fr.L: [Au] temps où [tu es] brisée par les mers, dans les profondeurs des eaux, \q tes marchandises et toute ta foule au milieu de toi sont tombées.
fr.B: Maintenant que tu es brisée par les mers, dans les profondeurs des eaux, \q tes marchandises et tout ton équipage ont sombré avec toi.
fr.R: Maintenant la mer t’a brisée, et tu es au fond de l’eau. \q Tes marchandises et tout ton équipage ont coulé avec toi.

decisions.choice: the time you are broken: now that you are wrecked
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins "time", meaning "at the time when". Some ancient translations read "now", which differs only in its vowels (stated from general knowledge). The sense is the same: the ship is now wrecked.

source.text: כֹּ֚ל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאִיִּ֔ים שָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלָ֑יִךְ וּמַלְכֵיהֶם֙ שָׂ֣עֲרוּ שַׂ֔עַר רָעֲמ֖וּ פָּנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: All [the] inhabitants of the coastlands are appalled over you, and their kings shudder [with] shuddering; troubled [are their] faces.

en.L: All the inhabitants of the coastlands are appalled over you, \q and their kings shudder with horror; \q [their] faces are troubled.
en.B: All who live on the coastlands are appalled at your fate; \q their kings shudder with horror, \q and their faces are twisted with fear.
en.R: Everyone who lives in lands far away across the sea is shocked at what happened to you. \q Their kings shake with horror, \q and their faces show their fear.

fr.L: Tous les habitants des îles sont consternés à ton sujet, \q et leurs rois frissonnent d’horreur ; \q [leurs] visages sont bouleversés.
fr.B: Tous les habitants des îles lointaines sont consternés par ton sort ; \q leurs rois frissonnent d’horreur, \q et leurs visages sont défigurés par la peur.
fr.R: Tous ceux qui vivent dans les pays lointains, de l’autre côté de la mer, sont choqués par ce qui t’est arrivé. \q Leurs rois tremblent d’horreur, \q et la peur se voit sur leurs visages.

decisions.choice: their kings shudder with horror: the verb is doubled
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the noun beside its verb ("shudder a shuddering") for emphasis (compare 32:10).

decisions.choice: lands far away across the sea
decisions.reason: Readable follows the Isaiah table for *iyyim*.

source.text: סֹֽחֲרִים֙ בָּ֣עַמִּ֔ים שָׁרְק֖וּ עָלָ֑יִךְ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔ית וְאֵינֵ֖ךְ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] traders among [the] peoples hiss over you; sudden terrors you have become, and you will not [be] until perpetuity.

en.L: The traders among the peoples hiss over you; \q sudden terrors you have become, \q and you will be no more forever."
en.B: The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; \q you have come to a terrifying end, \q and you will be no more forever."
en.R: The merchants of other nations whistle in shock at you. \q You have come to a horrible end, \q and you will be gone forever."

fr.L: Les marchands parmi les peuples sifflent sur toi ; \q tu es devenue des terreurs soudaines, \q et tu ne [seras] plus, à jamais. »
fr.B: Les marchands des peuples sifflent sur toi ; \q tu as connu une fin terrifiante, \q et tu ne seras plus jamais. »
fr.R: Les marchands des autres nations sifflent de stupeur en te voyant. \q Tu as connu une fin horrible, \q et tu as disparu pour toujours. »

decisions.choice: hiss: a sound of shock and scorn
decisions.reason: People hissed or whistled at a ruined place, in horror and contempt (1 Kings 9:8; Jeremiah 19:8).

decisions.choice: the refrain of the Tyre oracles
decisions.reason: The lament ends with the words that end 26:21 and 28:19.

decisions.choice: whistle in shock (R); hiss (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the hissing expressed.
